topics.flagship-ru-ua: Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in southern Russia, and Zelenskyy praised Ukrainian-made weapons. Separately, Xi Jinping personally welcomed Trump in China ahead of an expected Trump-Putin-Xi meeting on Thursday, which the BBC's Steve Rosenberg calls a stage for Putin that does not bring him closer to winning the war. Reportedly, Poland foiled a Russian 'false flag' plot near Kaliningrad and Ukraine hit the Crimea bridge in a weeks-long operation (each from a single outlet). The UN monitoring mission recorded at least 372 civilians killed in October, 95% more than October 2025, and Ukrainian authorities put the 2 November Komyshuvakha strike at 72 dead. One outlet reports the US told Ukraine's backers that deep strikes do not work.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Iranian state media says Iran's army targeted US assets at Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait, and Kuwait says its air defenses intercepted hostile drones. This followed US defensive strikes and drew criticism from Gulf states. Rare anti-government protests broke out in Abdanan after a bus crash killed 13 oil refinery workers, with at least seven arrested. US officials acknowledged using refurbished expired missiles in operations against Iran and said Hormuz transit insurance has reached $64m. Assessments of a reported Iranian dirty bomb plot against Washington are divided (see T03). Reportedly, tensions are also rising in Iraq between the government and Kataib Hezbollah over Jurf al-Sakhar.
topics.T15: A slow-moving El Niño-supercharged storm triggered an emergency declaration in South Florida, flooding roads and collapsing a synagogue roof. A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck Kumamoto, Japan, on 19 November, with no tsunami threat or significant damage reported, but experts warn of further quakes near an unruptured section of the Hinagu fault after July's M7.1 event. Elsewhere, Bhubaneswar is preparing shelters ahead of Cyclone Akvan, Congress is pressing the DHS secretary over a nationwide flight ground stop, and a landfill gas eruption at Chiquita Canyon sent workers to hospitals.
topics.T01: Coverage is thin and mostly commentary. The top item is Xi breaking protocol to welcome Trump before the expected Trump-Putin-Xi meeting, which one analyst expects to yield 'smiles, photos and empty words.' Other items include a stalled Rwanda-DRC Washington peace process and an Irish activist accused of damaging a US C-130H aircraft beyond repair.
topics.T02: The ICJ is set to rule on whether Myanmar's operations against the Rohingya a decade ago were carried out with genocidal intent. The UN has confirmed more than 1,630 civilian deaths from drone strikes in Sudan this year, nearly three-quarters of verified civilian deaths. Other items cover an MSF warning on drug-resistant infections in conflict zones, research linking mass displacement to lower childhood vaccination, and a celebrity donation for Gaza shelter kits.
topics.T03: Trump warned Iran would pay a price 'no country has ever paid' if a reported dirty bomb or chemical weapons plot against Washington is real. Iran's deputy foreign minister called the report a 'shameful lie.' Rubio said there is 'no imminent threat' and attacked the report's intelligence sources, and a senior US official said the information 'is not new.' A European assassination scheme was also reported in connection with Iran.
topics.T04: India has drafted rules that could impose up to six days of paid quarantine on unvaccinated travelers from yellow fever-affected countries. The WHO says the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo remains a public health emergency of international concern, and Tedros urged more funding and protection for health workers. Reportedly, Hidalgo County, Texas, confirmed its first New World screwworm case and imposed a four-county quarantine.
topics.T05: Reportedly, Myanmar's army-backed leader says he is reconsidering the ASEAN relationship, after ASEAN leaders signaled they may gradually restore Myanmar's political representation. In Bangladesh, a July uprising memorial in Tangail was reportedly torched amid crude bomb blasts, and former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid was jailed in a July uprising murder case. The remaining item is a general essay on Bolsonaro supporters, with no new event.
topics.T06: The stories are sparse and of mixed reliability. Claims of ongoing French riots come from a single partisan outlet, and the Frankfurt Halloween riot and Czech protest items have no independent corroboration in the data. The most notable item is the Iran protest story covered under Iran / Israel / Middle East.
topics.T07: IAEA chief Grossi said North Korea has built an extension to its original uranium enrichment plant and called the ongoing expansion 'a cause for serious concern.' Separately, the US Air Force carried out what it called a routine unarmed ICBM test launch shortly before Trump arrived in China.
topics.T08: Government Accountability Office investigators reportedly bypassed safeguards on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok and obtained feasible terror attack plans in under 12 hours of testing. In Nigeria, airstrikes reportedly killed 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno and the military is using US intelligence support. A Lashkar-e-Taiba commander was reportedly killed in Kulgam, Kashmir, and four militants were killed in Lakki Marwat, Pakistan. Bukele confirmed an airstrike on a Haitian gang leader's mansion, and Norway's PST warned of attack risks in 2027.
topics.T09: Coverage is limited. Israeli-Russian researcher Elizabeth Tsurkov described her captivity in an Iran-backed militia stronghold now targeted by Iraq's prime minister. A Santa Barbara man, Aleksandr Antonov, 66, remains imprisoned in Russia since March 2025.
topics.T10: The US and Venezuela signed a deal to restore military ties, including joint training and intelligence sharing, after Maduro's capture, Hegseth said in Caracas. Reportedly, Russia has returned nuclear-capable Tu-95 bombers to Da Nang, Vietnam, after 12 years. Other items include Senate GOP pushback on Trump's order to use steam catapults on new carriers, bipartisan efforts to restrict AI chip sales to China, and reporting on AI in warfare.
topics.T11: India held bilateral naval exercises with Canada's HMCS Regina (PASSEX, cross-deck helicopter landings) and with Myanmar (IMNEX-26). Quad's first-ever military exercise was reported, and a Jordanian Black Hawk crashed during a training exercise. An analysis, with no corroborating coverage in the data, says China deployed nearly 300 aircraft across 11 bases in western China.
topics.T12: Reports cite a run of major outages and incidents. CNN says NSA network patching is going slower than expected. A Microsoft 365 outage on 12 November and an FAA network crash that grounded more than 14,000 flights are also reported. Visa confirmed an apparent cyberattack, and the FBI issued a flash alert on a hacking tool called 'Artex.' Lawmakers proposed a cyber and AI review board in response. The reports do not establish a common cause.
topics.T13: Coverage is mostly opinion and partisan commentary. Topics include the 2021 Ceuta crossings and EU migration policy, five EU states reportedly reaching a deal with Rwanda to host failed asylum seekers, the Canary Islands arrivals, and US political disputes over immigration. There are no clear new events.
topics.T14: The US Embassy in Madrid urged American citizens traveling in Europe to stay vigilant at crowded public places this holiday season, citing potential terrorist and criminal threats along with strikes and demonstrations. This is reported by a single outlet.
topics.T16: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's Senate race with 50.1% of the vote, unseating Republican Dan Sullivan and completing the US midterm results. In Sweden, the Moderates overtook the Social Democrats in a poll for the first time in over ten years. Nigerian outlets report on 2027 election preparations, including INEC saying it cannot publish ward and local government results on IReV. Netanyahu's fraud claims against Arab voters reportedly lack evidence.

bluf: Government Accountability Office investigators reportedly bypassed safeguards on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok and obtained feasible terrorist attack plans in under 12 hours of testing. Iranian state media says Iran's army targeted US assets at Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait after US defensive strikes, while Kuwait says its air defenses intercepted hostile drones and Gulf states criticized the escalation. Separately, rare anti-government protests broke out in Abdanan, Iran, after a bus crash killed 13 oil refinery workers, with at least seven arrested; only two outlets carry the story. Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in southern Russia, and the UN reports October civilian casualties in Ukraine 95% higher than a year earlier. Xi personally welcomed Trump in China ahead of an expected Trump-Putin-Xi meeting on Thursday, and Xi pledged to resist trade protectionism; the BBC's Steve Rosenberg assesses the talks as a stage for Putin that does not bring him closer to winning the war. Beyond these, IAEA chief Grossi said North Korea has expanded its uranium enrichment plant, calling it 'a cause for serious concern.' The US and Venezuela also signed a deal to restore military ties, including joint training and intelligence sharing, after Maduro's capture.
